companyDescription: eVTOL Air Taxi · First manufacturer to complete FAA Type Certification Phase 3 of 4 · Acquiring Boeing's Wisk Aero, Insitu & SkyGrid (antitrust cleared Sep 2026) · $1.56B cash cushion
priceNote: Live $3.81 (-2.6%) at Oct 26, 2026 open — down ~26% from $5.18 at the Sep 29 report, at a fresh 52-week low ($3.68-$11.72). Market cap ~$2.93B on 770M shares. Since the Sep 29 reports, this board's small caps fell 21-41% after the Sep 16 hike and the hot Sep CPI (Oct 14). This is a sector/size selloff that SPY-based regime notes don't capture, so drawdowns here say as much about the tape as the thesis.
summary: REFRESH (prior report Sep 29, 2026): ACHR fell ~26% to a new 52-week low with no change in the thesis — first eVTOL through FAA Type Certification Phase 3 of 4, Wisk/Insitu/SkyGrid closing slated for year-end, piloted Bay Area flights and announced Texas networks. ARK added ~$12.1M of stock in early October. Q3 earnings (Nov 9) are the dated read on burn (Q2 net loss $263.2M) and the Phase 4 timeline. regulatory_approval is a Tier-2 LEADER (+5.3pp vs +2.0pp, n=8). Survival is not an issue (~$1.5B+ liquidity). Base trimmed from +60% to +45% (above the lane's realized 30d P90 of +25.9%; written-Base bias +72.7pp). It assumes 3-6 months with a Phase 4 update and the Wisk close. แนะนำ 2-3% ของ portfolio เท่านั้น — ถ้า thesis fail ลงได้ 40-60%.

catalysts.name: Q3 2026 Earnings
catalysts.description: Cash burn (Q2 net loss $263.2M), liquidity, the FAA Phase 4 timeline, and Wisk/Insitu/SkyGrid closing status.

catalysts.name: FAA Type Certification — Phase 4 (final)
catalysts.description: First eVTOL maker through Phase 3 of 4. Recent piloted Bay Area flights and announced Texas networks (Austin, DFW, Houston); commercial ops under the eIPP pilot program targeted for 2026.

catalysts.name: Boeing Wisk / Insitu / SkyGrid acquisition close
catalysts.description: Antitrust cleared Sep 2026; closing slated for year-end pending remaining approvals. Adds Wisk's autonomous Gen 6 aircraft.

risks: Pre-revenue: TTM revenue ~$6.9M against a ~$800M TTM net loss. The thesis is entirely certification and commercialization timing.
Rate-sensitive, high-beta stock: it has repeatedly sold off on rising Treasury yields, even with ample cash.
No confirmed FAA Phase 4 timeline yet; 2026 commercial-launch targets could slip into 2027.
The Wisk/Insitu/SkyGrid acquisition still needs remaining regulatory approvals, and integrating three Boeing subsidiaries is complex.
A single eVTOL safety incident, Archer's or a competitor's, would hit the whole sector.

macroRisk.rateOutlook: Fed funds at 3.75-4.00% after the surprise Sep 16, 2026 hike (first since 2023). The Oct 27-28 FOMC is priced ~93% hold / ~7% +25bp as of Oct 25 — but hike odds briefly spiked to ~44% after the hot Sep CPI print on Oct 14, so the path stays two-sided.
macroRisk.inflationNote: September CPI +0.6% m/m, 3.7% y/y headline; core +0.3% m/m, 2.6% y/y — both above consensus. Headline re-acceleration keeps a further 2026 hike live.
macroRisk.sectorImpact: Well-funded but pre-revenue and high-beta. ACHR has repeatedly traded on Treasury yields, so a hawkish surprise hits the multiple even though solvency isn't in question.
macroRisk.summary: MEDIUM — Oct 28 hold is priced (~93%), but hot CPI keeps a further 2026 hike live. Small, cash-burning names have already absorbed most of this tape's damage, so a hold is mildly supportive and a surprise hike is the main macro tail.

entryStrategy.verdict: SPECULATIVE · Moonshot 2.5% max (refreshed Oct 26) — a Tier-2-leader regulatory catalyst with no survival risk, priced at a 52-week low. Measured turbo at-catalyst median is -13.7% (n=19), so Entry 2 ($3.30-3.60) is preferred and Entry 1 is a starter only.

catalystSpot.preRunup: No run-up: ACHR fell ~26% since Sep 29 to a new 52-week low, even as ARK bought ~2.57M shares (~$12.1M) in early October.

postWin.note: Full FAA Type Certification (Phase 4) remains the single biggest catalyst in company history — no eVTOL company has completed this yet, so Archer as first mover is the reference case. This is unchanged from the last report; per turbo.tier2, regulatory_approval is a LEADER type (medianExcessVsBenchPct +5.3pp vs overall +2.0pp, n=8), supporting this sizing.
postWin.exampleDate: No direct historical comp — first mover

postLose.note: A major Phase 4 delay, a sector-wide safety incident, or the Boeing deal collapsing on remaining regulatory approvals would likely trigger a sharp de-rate. The recent -7% single-day move on rising yields alone shows how quickly sentiment can turn even without company-specific bad news.

spotSizing.reason: 2.5%. regulatory_approval is a Tier-2 LEADER (+5.3pp median excess vs SPY vs +2.0pp, n=8; 2/8 windows had SPY down >2%), and the ~$1.5B+ cash pile removes near-term survival risk. The weak lane scoreboard (hitRate 4.9%, n=41) and an undated Phase 4 keep it below 3%.

stopPreCatalyst.note: Wider than the regulatory_approval medianMAE (-25.0%, n=8). A break below ~$2.74 means the market is pricing a certification slip or a raise.

stopPostCatalyst.note: If Q3 pushes certification or commercial launch into late 2027, or announces a large discounted raise, exit.

comparableCases.note: Same-day +4.02% reaction to becoming the first eVTOL manufacturer to complete Phase 3 — direct evidence of how the market reacts to certification-phase milestones; full Type Certification (Phase 4) should be a materially larger version of this same reaction.

comparableCases.event: Rising Treasury yields hit eVTOL/speculative growth names
comparableCases.note: Recent, direct evidence of macro rate-sensitivity — a pure sentiment/multiple-compression move, not thesis-driven, but real and worth sizing around given the current hawkish-Fed backdrop.
